name: turn
comment: The chat's turn record (app/src/PrismTurn.lex.tex): what its person said to the Prism as one W3C EMMA 1.0 document, and the turn as one W3C PROV-N document (the person and the Prism as agents, the turn as an activity that used the prompt and each thing the reply drew on, the reply generated by it and derived from them, the turn informed by the one before). The guest is built from PrismTurn, PrismEmma, PrismProv and the annotation facet's PrismCite, so a record is judged by the same checkers that hold the Recommendation's EMMA documents, W3C's PROV constraint cases and the W3C annotation-model suite. A cited line that also says where in the reply's text its words were taken (start and end, in code points) adds one line to the record: the W3C Web Annotation the cite facet writes for that stretch of the reply, whose address is the SHA-256 of its text, and that thing. An act line names the dimension of what was said as a dialogue act (ISO 24617-2: task, autoFeedback or socialObligationsManagement, as the router read it) and is kept on the prompt as the attribute me:dimension; anything else is refused. An identity line names the person's card as the senses guest observed it (sha256: and the SHA-256 of their vCard's bytes) and is kept as an entity attributed to the person, which the turn used; anything else is refused. 'record' and its lines (base, now, after, prompt, reply, act, identity, cited) answers the EMMA document, a line end and then the PROV-N document, or 'refused: ' and why; nothing is answered that either checker faults. 'check' and a record answers 'accepted', or 'refused: ' and the standard it breaks. 'examples' are the acceptance vectors: each a 'check' of a record put together from W3C's own documents, an EMMA document of the Recommendation as the emma guest's vectors hold it and a PROV-N case of W3C's constraint suite, with the verdict W3C's case carries (PASS accepted, FAIL refused). The last five add citations: annotations as the cite facet's own vectors give them (built outside LexLean, accepted by the suite's validator) are accepted, and a line the suite's musts do not accept is refused. 'sources' names the specs those bytes are taken from, each pinned there by SHA-256.

gaps.why: No authoritative source gives the expected answer of 'record': EMMA and PROV define what a well-formed record is, not which record a turn of this chat makes. So no 'record' request is an acceptance vector; what holds for every 'record' answer is that both checkers accepted it inside the guest before it was answered, and the cases under 'shape' only show the request grammar. Which PROV relations a chat turn should carry (used, wasDerivedFrom, wasInformedBy) is this model's reading of PROV-DM; ISO 24617-2's dialogue act and its dependence relations are not yet in the record.
